page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 206 and title "Animalium Mar. Ordo XIIII." Main text in two blocks: a full-width text column with a woodcut of a crab at upper left, and margin notes left ("Alius latipes", "Cursores.", "Equites."). Below, further text with woodcuts of a crab and a lobster-like crustacean, and a second crab woodcut with text to its right.

sunt, &c. hi quoq; nouissimos pedes in extremo latos habent.
eorum magnitudo pollice operiri potest: uiuaces tamen admo-

(inquit Rondeletius) locutum puto Aristotelem, ubi scribit: Parui Cancri qui capiuntur inter paruos
piscículos, postremos pedes habent latos, ut ad natandum sint utiles, & pinnarum uel
palmularum uice. ¶ Quærendum an hic Cancer sit, quem Cursorem cognominant.
Bellon. Cursores cãcros, eosdē Equitibus facit, nescio quā recte. Aristoteles diuersis in locis, nomi-nibus quoq;
diuersis eos commemorat. Cursores enim esse arbitror, quamuis ipse non nominat, Latipedes illos
quorum meminit De partibus animalium lib.4.c.8. Equitum uero mentionem facit Historiæ
4.2. Genus est quoddam Cancrorum (inquit) in litoribus Phœniciæ, tantæ velocitatis, ut uix
quisquam consequi possit: unde ἵππος, id est, Equites appellantur. ijs nihil ferè intus pro-
pter inopiam pabuli est. Δ, ὁμωῳ est paruus Cancer, Hesychius. Cancri ἀεομίαι (inquit Aelianus) longè lateq;

loca saxosa, uel cœnosa, cibum perquirentes, sæpe perueniunt. Bellonius in Singularibus scribit
hos Cancros non multò maiores esse castanea.
ITAL. Romæ Grancetto uocant, (forma diminutiua nimirum à Cancro.) Veneti ac Ferra-
rienses Mazenetam, (Hoc nomen etiam simpliciter Cancro marino paruo attribuunt, ut supra dictum est,)
Bellonius.
GALL. Massilienses Grittam genuina uoce nominant, Bellonius. Sed Maia etiam in Provin-
cia aliquibus Gritta uocatur.
GERM. F. Ein breitfüß/ Ein Leuffer/ Ein kleiner Meerkrabb/ hat die ij. letsten füß
breitlacht/ lauffrt schnell.
CANCER Flauus siue Vndulatus Rondeletij. Cancer hic (inquit) inter anonymos & ignobiles
magnus est, Cancris stagni marini uel fluuiatilibus æqualis. Flauum à colore nominauimus:
Vndulatum à lineis quæ in prona parte sunt sinuosæ undarum modo, non aliter quàm in camelloto
uulgò nuncupato. Capitur circa Antipolim & Lerinum insulam, nec uspiam similes uidi. Caudam
extentam depinximus, &c.

page.notes: Margin notes left: "Alius latipes" (beside first crab woodcut), "Cursores." and "Equites." Greek and Hebrew-like characters in the text are transcribed as best read; the Greek phrase after "Cancri" and "Δ, ὁμωῳ" are doubtful. Several words in the German lines and the Greek are uncertain. The page ends mid-sentence at "Sole", continuing on the next page. Engravings: crab woodcut (upper left), a large crustacean woodcut (centre), and a mottled crab woodcut (lower left).
